scope: Proposition 4.4 (Positive mass on every interval) of the manuscript “An exact Hausdorff gauge for SLE” (preprints/An-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-25-2026/An-exact-Hausdorff-gauge-for-SLE-September-25-2026.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 230 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 513ca9aedce0f342), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 20. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Almost surely, for every 0 ≤ v < t < ∞, (µt − µv)(H) > 0. The positive mass can always be detected on an interior compact. The same statement holds in every fixed conformal image, in its associated half-plane time.
